before: switch(value) compares its value against case expressions using strict equality. A matching case starts execution there. It does not automatically stop at the next case label; without break or return, execution can fall through.

Implement delivery(kind) with grouped letter/card cases returning "small", parcel returning "large", and all other inputs returning "unknown". Match exact strings.
after:
`switch(value)` looks for a matching `case` using strict equality. Once a case matches, execution starts there.

It can continue into the next case unless `break`, `return`, or another stopping action ends it. This is called fall-through.

Put `"letter"` and `"card"` before the same return so they share `"small"`. A parcel returns `"large"`; `default` handles anything else.

`return` leaves the function, so these cases do not also need `break`.

Adjacent case labels can share one action on purpose. If a case only assigns a value, use `break` when it should not continue into the next case.

Matching is exact: text `"1"` does not match the number 1.
Build `delivery(kind)` with the grouped letter/card cases, the parcel case, and a default. Keep the exact spelling of each accepted string.
